findings.title: [P1] Remove unsupported `--dfs-lvl-t-ck-*` flags from CLI test
findings.body: `gen_timing_params` does not define any `--dfs-lvl-t-ck-*` arguments, so every CLI invocation built here exits in `argparse` before it can write a binary. Because `generate_random_params()` now always adds all three DFS fields, `test_random_param_comparison()` will fail on every iteration instead of exercising GUI/CLI parity.

findings.title: [P1] Restore random fixtures to generator-valid timing combos
findings.body: This change replaces the previous curated LPDDR4/LPDDR5 timing profiles with unconstrained random values, so the new comparison loop now spends most runs failing input validation instead of comparing binaries. Even with the unsupported DFS flags removed, these samples frequently trip generator checks such as `invalid target clock period` and LPDDR5 WCK-always-on constraints, which makes the 100-iteration test largely unusable.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve common timing fields in the analysis response
findings.body: Any binary opened in the analysis modal now loses `tlp_resp`, `dll_enable`, ODT/DBI, and postamble settings entirely: `parse_timing_entries()` always returns `common = {}`, while the template still renders those values only from `timing_entries.common` and only `wck_ratio` was moved into the per-entry table. The result is an empty "Common Params" section and no remaining place to inspect those parsed fields.

overall_explanation: The patch introduces two regressions in the new GUI/CLI parity test: the generated CLI command now includes unsupported DFS options, and the random fixture generator no longer stays within the tool's valid parameter space. It also drops several parsed timing fields from the analysis UI by emptying the `common` payload without adding equivalent display coverage.
